The Wyoming Land Quality Division (WLQD) submitted this proposed amendment in response to our January 19, 2024 partial approval of an amendment to WLQD's regulations for coal exploration by drilling (SATS No. WY-050-FOR; Docket ID No. OSM-2021- 0004). In the final rule, under the heading \"Revisions to Wyoming's Rules That We Are Not Approving,\" OSM listed several provisions containing typographical errors that WLQD would need to correct through future rulemaking. WLQD now proposes those corrections with this amendment (SATS No. WY-055-FOR; Docket ID No. OSM-2025-0002).","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21825","title":"Sunshine Act Meetings","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21825/sunshine-act-meetings","summary":"","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21823","title":"Senior Executive Service (SES) Performance Review Board; Notice of Membership","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21823/senior-executive-service-ses-performance-review-board-notice-of-membership","summary":"This notice announces the appointment of members to the Performance Review Board (PRB) for the National Endowment for the Arts (NEA). The PRB is responsible for reviewing the performance appraisals of Senior Executive Service (SES) members and making recommendations regarding performance ratings, pay adjustments, and bonuses to ensure consistency, fairness, and adherence to Office of Personnel Management (OPM) regulations and agency policies.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21822","title":"Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21822/submission-for-omb-review-comment-request","summary":"","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21821","title":"Enhancing the Ability of Consumers To Control the Robocalls","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21821/enhancing-the-ability-of-consumers-to-control-the-robocalls","summary":"In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) modifies rules to ensure that consumers can revoke consent for robocalls they no longer wish to receive while continuing to receive those they still want. We also modernize our rules to ensure that consumers have clear, simple, and automated ways to revoke consent while streamlining callers' ability to process revocations. Specifically, we allow callers to interpret a revocation request as applying only to the specific category of informational robocalls to which the revocation was directed, allow callers to designate an exclusive means to revoke consent, and amend the exemption from the consent requirement for financial institutions to allow them to more easily alert customers to fraudulent activity on their account. In addition, we delegate authority to the Consumer and Governmental Affairs Bureau (CGB) in consultation with the Enforcement Bureau (EB) to review our robocall rules to ensure that those rules are clear and easy to read.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21820","title":"Modernizing the Ability of Consumers To Control Robocalls","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21820/modernizing-the-ability-of-consumers-to-control-robocalls","summary":"In this document, the Commission seeks comment on measures to ensure that the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) rules that govern robocalls continue to evolve with changes in technology and industry practices. Specifically, we seek comment on reducing the timeframe callers must honor revocation requests, requirements for two- way texting functionality, requiring a revoke all method, and the treatment of affiliates.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21819","title":"Certain Small Vertical Shaft Engines Between 99cc and up to 225cc, and Parts Thereof From the People's Republic of China: Continuation of Antidumping and Countervailing Duty Orders","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21819/certain-small-vertical-shaft-engines-between-99cc-and-up-to-225cc-and-parts-thereof-from-the-peoples","summary":"As a result of the determinations by the U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) and the U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) that revocation of the antidumping duty (AD) and countervailing duty (CVD) orders on certain small vertical shaft engines between 99cc and 225cc, and parts thereof (small vertical engines) from the People's Republic of China (China) would likely lead to the continuation or recurrence of dumping, countervailable subsidies, and material injury to an industry in the United States, Commerce is publishing a notice of continuation of these AD and CVD orders.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21818","title":"Space Modernization for the 21st Century","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21818/space-modernization-for-the-21st-century","summary":"In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission or we) adopts a Further Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (FNPRM) that seeks comment on and/or proposes additional reforms.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21817","title":"Establishment of Class E Airspace; Canton, IL","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21817/establishment-of-class-e-airspace-canton-il","summary":"This action establishes Class E airspace at Graham Hospital Heliport, Canton, IL. Stewart Petroleum Products, Inc., USDOT # 1290158","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21812/parts-and-accessories-necessary-for-safe-operation-application-for-an-exemption-from-rb-stewart","summary":"FMCSA requests public comment on an application from R.B. Stewart Petroleum Products, Inc., USDOT No. 1290158, (R.B. Stewart) for an exemption from the requirement that lighting devices be steady burning. The exemption would allow the company to operate commercial motor vehicles (CMVs) equipped with a module manufactured by Intellistop, Inc. (Intellistop) which pulses the rear clearance, identification, and brake lamps from low-level lighting intensity to high-level lighting intensity 4 times in 2 seconds when the brakes are applied, and then return the lights to a steady-burning state while the brakes remain engaged. FMCSA requests public comment on the applicant's request for exemption.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21811","title":"Information Collection Being Reviewed by the Federal Communications Commission","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21811/information-collection-being-reviewed-by-the-federal-communications-commission","summary":"As part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork burdens, and as required by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA), the Federal Communications Commission (FCC or Commission) invites the general public and other Federal agencies to take this opportunity to comment on the following information collections. Comments are requested concerning: whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the Commission, including whether the information shall have practical utility; the accuracy of the Commission's burden estimate; ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information collected; ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on the respondents, including the use of automated collection techniques or other forms of information technology; and ways to further reduce the information collection burden on small business concerns with fewer than 25 employees. The FCC may not conduct or sponsor a collection of information unless it displays a currently valid Office of Management and Budget (OMB) control number. No person shall be subject to any penalty for failing to comply with a collection of information subject to the PRA that does not display a valid OMB control number.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21810","title":"Petition for Reconsideration of Action in Rulemaking Proceeding","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21810/petition-for-reconsideration-of-action-in-rulemaking-proceeding","summary":"Petition for Reconsideration (Petition) has been filed in the Commission's proceeding by Harold Feld on behalf of Public Knowledge and others.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21809","title":"Information Collection Being Submitted for Review and Approval to Office of Management and Budget","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21809/information-collection-being-submitted-for-review-and-approval-to-office-of-management-and-budget","summary":"As part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork burdens, as required by the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) of 1995, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC or the Commission) invites the general public and other Federal Agencies to take this opportunity to comment on the following information collection. Pursuant to the Small Business Paperwork Relief Act of 2002, the FCC seeks specific comment on how it can further reduce the information collection burden for small business concerns with fewer than 25 employees.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21808","title":"Closed Captioning of Video Programming","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21808/closed-captioning-of-video-programming","summary":"In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) exempts video programmers for public, educational, and governmental access (PEG) channels from the requirement to register with the Commission and to certify captioning compliance if the PEG video programmers provide video programming exclusively to PEG channels that are exempt from closed captioning requirements. Additionally, providers of PEG programming are relieved of filing obligations if the administrators of non-exempt PEG channels certify compliance for programming carried on such channels. The Commission similarly exempts providers of programming carried on nonbroadcast networks for distribution by a cable operator or other multichannel video programming distributor (MVPD) from certifying when the nonbroadcast network itself certifies that it is exempt or that all programming comprising the network's linear line-up is either exempt from or compliant with the closed captioning rules.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-21807","title":"Ohio Regulatory Program","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/26/2026-21807/ohio-regulatory-program","summary":"The Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement (OSM) is approving an amendment to the Ohio regulatory program (Ohio program) under the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 (SMCRA or the Act). OSM is approving Ohio's proposal to add, rescind, or modify 39 rules under the Ohio Administrative Code that relate to, among other things: permit applications, hydrologic map and cross-sections, general map requirements, requirements for permits for special categories of mining, underground mining permit application, small operator assistance program, and self-bonding.","publishedAt":"2026-10-26","source":"Federal Register"}]}
